plan.title: Ember Roasters: Fresh Coffee Every Two Weeks
plan.description: Ember Roasters is a coffee subscription of small-batch beans roasted to order and shipped every two weeks. Pause or cancel anytime, and your first bag is 50% off.

beats.narration: What if your coffee was roasted only for you? Not months ago, not on a warehouse shelf. This morning, in a small batch, just for your order. That's the idea behind Ember Roasters.
Every bag is small-batch, roasted to order. Pick a roast, pick a rhythm. We grind to your liking, and the beans ship within days of leaving the cooling tray.
Your coffee arrives every two weeks. First, choose your roast. Second, we roast it fresh. Third, it lands at your door, right on schedule, ready to brew.
Life changes, so your plan can too. Pause when you're away. Cancel anytime. You stay in control of every delivery.
And right now, your first bag is fifty percent off. Try Ember Roasters today. Fresh, small-batch coffee, roasted to order, waiting for your first cup.

accuracy.reason: Core offer facts match the brief, but "grind to your liking" and "within days of leaving the cooling tray" come from a third-party site's notes, not the brief. "This morning" for every order is an overclaim.

coverage.reason: All brief points are present (small-batch, roasted to order, two weeks, pause/cancel, 50% off). The problem of stale coffee is only lightly touched, and there is no real CTA such as a URL or "subscribe".

structure.reason: Clear flow from hook to benefits, how it works, flexibility and offer. The two-week cadence is repeated in beats 3 and 4.

hook_ending.reason: "What if your coffee was roasted only for you?" is a decent hook. The ending is a soft "waiting for your first cup" with no concrete action step.

tone.reason: Warm, upbeat promo voice that suits the brief.

visuals.reason: Scene types vary and match the narration. Three bullet/step/checklist scenes in a row feel template-like, and there is little imagery beyond the opening clip.

originality.reason: Some nice phrases ("Not months ago, not on a warehouse shelf"), but the rest is generic promo copy such as "Life changes, so your plan can too".

instructions.reason: Covers every brief item and uses the brand name. The script is about 120 words, close to the target, and the video runs about a minute. It adds claims not in the brief.

defects.quote: This morning, in a small batch, just for your order.
defects.issue: Claims same-morning roasting, which is not in the brief and contradicts the later "ship within days"; it is an invented specific.

defects.quote: We grind to your liking, and the beans ship within days of leaving the cooling tray.
defects.issue: Taken from a third-party site's notes and not in the brief, so it is an unrequested claim.
The call to action is vague, with no link, button or "start your subscription" instruction.

defects.quote: Your coffee arrives every two weeks.
defects.issue: The cadence is repeated in beats 3 and 4 (scenes and narration), which wastes time in a short promo.

defects.quote: Not months ago, not on a warehouse shelf.
defects.issue: The stale-coffee problem gets one line and is never developed.

missing: Clear call to action (URL or sign-up prompt)
Mention that the 50% discount applies only to the first bag, stated plainly
wrong_facts: "This morning" roasting for each order is unsupported by the brief
Grind-to-order and cooling-tray details come from an unrelated site, not the brief
judge.summary: A clean, on-brief promo with all key offer points and fluent copy. It adds unsupported claims such as same-morning roasting, has a weak CTA, and leans on template-style scenes.
